title: E228｜谷歌TPU能撼动英伟达吗？前TPU工程师首次揭秘
title_en: E228 | Can Google's TPU Shake Nvidia? A Former TPU Engineer Reveals All
eyebrow: AI Infrastructure & Chips · AI 算力与芯片
summary_cn: 前谷歌TPU工程师Henry Zhu（2018–2024，参与V6/V7/V8研发）首次系统拆解：TPU是流水线式矩阵加速器、GPU是并行大厨；在限定条件下（大规模部署、模型形态稳定）TPU的TCO可挑战英伟达，但XLA黑盒生态、HBM/CoWoS产能与ASIC押注方向是三大命门
summary_en: Former Google TPU engineer Henry Zhu — who worked from 2018 to 2024 on the V6, V7, and V8 — breaks down the architecture for the first time: TPUs are pipeline-style matrix accelerators, while GPUs are parallel chefs. Under limited conditions like large-scale deployment and stable model architectures, the TPU's total cost of ownership can challenge Nvidia. But three vulnerabilities remain: the black-box XLA ecosystem, HBM and CoWoS capacity, and the risky bet of ASIC specialization.

scenes.title_en: TPU vs GPU: The Fundamental Architectural Difference
scenes.context: 用厨房比喻解释 GPU 与 TPU 的架构差异，以及 TPU 高利用率的原因。语域：casual 技术科普 + formal 分析。
scenes.speak: The core mechanism: GPUs come from gaming graphics cards and use a SIMT multi-thread architecture — like a kitchen full of independent chefs, each grabbing ingredients, cooking, and plating on their own, with massively parallel compute. The TPU is a custom accelerator built for matrix computation, like an assembly-line relay: the first person grabs ingredients, the second processes, the third plates, with minimal scheduling in between and higher device utilization. The key insight: modern pretraining has shifted from compute-bound to memory-bound. GPUs idle while waiting for data movement when computing grain by grain; TPUs use software-hardware co-design to stay at full power — either reusing cached data or saturating memory bandwidth. A typical scene: large-scale Transformer pretraining and Gemini-class custom model training. As the episode put it, GPUs are like multiple chefs working in parallel independently; TPUs are like a pipeline relay, pumping results to every corner like a heart pumping blood, with far less scheduling in the middle. Compared with Groq's LPU: Groq is a compiler company, and its hardware serves deterministic low latency; the TPU is a system-level cluster solution that excels at high throughput rather than tail latency. When deeply customized for Google's own Gemini or frontier models from big labs, once all assumptions are fixed, the TPU beats the GPU in training efficiency and total cost of ownership. The core reason is better utilization: software tells the hardware what to do at every tick, the hardware layer adds no complex control units, and all complexity goes to XLA.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：GPU源于游戏显卡，SIMT多线程架构——像厨房里安排很多大厨，每人独立从冰箱取料、做菜、上菜，并行算力极强。TPU是面向矩阵计算的定制加速器，像流水线接力：第一人取菜、第二人加工、第三人装盘，中间调度极少，设备利用率更高
sentences.en: The core mechanism: GPUs come from gaming graphics cards and use a SIMT multi-thread architecture — like a kitchen full of independent chefs, each grabbing ingredients, cooking, and plating on their own, with massively parallel compute. The TPU is a custom accelerator built for matrix computation, like an assembly-line relay: the first person grabs ingredients, the second processes, the third plates, with minimal scheduling in between and higher device utilization.
sentences.note: 表达提示SIMT（Single Instruction, Multiple Threads）→ 单指令多线程；parallel compute → 并行算力；device utilization → 设备利用率

sentences.cn: 关键理解：现代预训练从compute bound转向memory bound，GPU逐粒计算时会有idle period等待数据搬运；TPU通过软硬件协同保证满功率运行，要么复用缓存数据，要么跑满内存带宽
sentences.en: The key insight: modern pretraining has shifted from compute-bound to memory-bound. GPUs idle while waiting for data movement when computing grain by grain; TPUs use software-hardware co-design to stay at full power — either reusing cached data or saturating memory bandwidth.
sentences.note: 表达提示compute-bound / memory-bound → 算力受限/带宽受限；idle period → 空闲期；saturate memory bandwidth → 跑满内存带宽

sentences.en: When deeply customized for Google's own Gemini or frontier models from big labs, once all assumptions are fixed, the TPU beats the GPU in training efficiency and total cost of ownership. The core reason is better utilization: software tells the hardware what to do at every tick, the hardware layer adds no complex control units, and all complexity goes to XLA.

scenes.title_en: Capacity Bottlenecks: HBM, CoWoS, and Yield Rates
scenes.context: HBM 供给垄断、CoWoS 封装产能与定制芯片良率的生死线。语域：formal 供应链分析。
scenes.speak: The first reason: the HBM market is monopolized by SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron, and Nvidia has always been the biggest customer; the TPU is a second-rate customer in the supply chain, struggling to lock in orders at Nvidia's scale. The fix: Anthropic's million-chip order plus external orders from Meta and others help Google lock in more capacity with Broadcom, TSMC, and HBM makers. How serious? Fatal — the industry has moved from compute-bound to memory-bound; if you can't buy good HBM, training efficiency takes a huge hit. As the guest said, capacity is locked one or two years ahead; without huge customer demand, you can't reshuffle on short notice — HBM is very hard to source. Another reason: 2.5D stacking packaging can only rely on TSMC's CoWoS capacity allocation; the TPU emphasizes chip-to-chip communication, has higher yield than GPUs, and can't degrade from H100 to A100 the way GPUs can — if a custom chip's yield is bad, the whole product is scrapped. The fix: external big-customer orders plus deep binding with Broadcom to win TSMC capacity priority.

sentences.cn: 原因：HBM市场被SK海力士、三星、美光三家垄断，英伟达一直是最大客户；TPU在供应链中处于second rate customer，难以锁定与英伟达同等量级订单
sentences.en: The reason: the HBM market is monopolized by SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron, and Nvidia has always been the biggest customer; the TPU is a second-rate customer in the supply chain, struggling to lock in orders at Nvidia's scale.
sentences.note: 表达提示HBM（High Bandwidth Memory）→ 高带宽内存；monopolize → 垄断；second-rate customer → 次级客户

sentences.cn: 解法：Anthropic百万颗订单+Meta等外部大单，帮助谷歌与Broadcom/TSMC/HBM厂商锁定更大产能
sentences.en: The fix: Anthropic's million-chip order plus external orders from Meta and others help Google lock in more capacity with Broadcom, TSMC, and HBM makers.
sentences.note: 表达提示lock in capacity → 锁定产能；external order → 外部大单；chip order → 芯片订单

sentences.cn: 严重程度：致命——行业已从compute bound进入memory bound，买不到好HBM训练效率大折扣
sentences.en: How serious? Fatal — the industry has moved from compute-bound to memory-bound; if you can't buy good HBM, training efficiency takes a huge hit.
sentences.note: 表达提示take a huge hit → 大打折扣；memory-bound era → 带宽受限时代

sentences.cn: （引用）嘉宾说法：「产能都是提前一两年锁定的，没有那么大客户需求就临时调不动；HBM非常难找货」
sentences.en: As the guest said: 'Capacity is locked one or two years ahead; without huge customer demand, you can't reshuffle on short notice — HBM is very hard to source.'

scenes.title_cn: 三、XLA软件黑盒与生态之争
scenes.title_en: The XLA Black Box and the Ecosystem War
scenes.context: XLA 编译器的系统级优化能力、黑盒困境与 CUDA 生态对比。语域：formal 技术生态分析。
scenes.speak: The core mechanism: XLA is a static compiler. When the workload is known, it can do system-level optimization across the global TPU pod — operator fusion, avoiding repeated memory round-trips for intermediate states, and customizing memory allocation for the hardware architecture. The upper layers support PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow, all translated into TPU assembly instructions. The key insight: compared with CUDA's open ecosystem, XLA is a black box — it can squeeze out performance, but developers can't easily control it; debugging requires understanding both hardware and software, and external customers can hardly fix bugs independently. A typical scene: Anthropic, whose team comes from Google and understands XLA; and Apple, where Pang Ruoming took the whole stack to train Apple Intelligence. As the episode put it, XLA is a black box and the secret sauce; external developers can hardly handle or fix a bug on their own and must reach out to Google engineers. Compared with CUDA: CUDA's ecosystem is mature and independently debuggable; XLA's performance ceiling is higher but the barrier is extremely high, and you must migrate to JAX plus XLA to unlock the TPU's advantages. The host then pressed: is it because many Anthropic engineers come from Google and are familiar with the XLA ecosystem? Henry confirmed that's one important factor, layered on top of Google's investment in-loop relationship, Anthropic's top engineering capability, and the reality that deploying TPUs is extremely hard for ordinary external customers.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：XLA是静态编译器，当Workload已知时可在全局TPU Pod做系统级优化：算子融合、中间态不反复存取内存、按硬件架构定制内存分配。上层支持PyTorch/JAX/TensorFlow，翻译成TPU汇编指令
sentences.en: The core mechanism: XLA is a static compiler. When the workload is known, it can do system-level optimization across the global TPU pod — operator fusion, avoiding repeated memory round-trips for intermediate states, and customizing memory allocation for the hardware architecture. The upper layers support PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow, all translated into TPU assembly instructions.
sentences.note: 表达提示static compiler → 静态编译器；operator fusion → 算子融合；TPU pod → 全局TPU集群

sentences.cn: 关键理解：对比CUDA开放生态，XLA是黑盒——能榨干性能但开发者难控制；debug需要同时懂硬件和软件，外部客户很难独立fix bug

sentences.note: 表达提示black box → 黑盒；squeeze out performance → 榨干性能；fix bugs independently → 独立修bug

scenes.title_cn: 四、大模型时代：MoE优化与方向押注
scenes.title_en: The LLM Era: MoE Optimization and Direction Bets
scenes.context: TPU 如何通过 3D 拓扑解决 MoE 痛点，以及激进定制的风险。语域：formal 芯片技术 + 战略判断。
scenes.speak: Early MoE didn't run well on TPUs, because in a 2D topology a chip can only talk to its neighbors, and routing to different experts required many detours. The V4 introduced a 3D Torus with an OCI optical switch, letting software program the communication paths, solving the MoE all-to-all pain point in one shot with a clear efficiency gain. As the episode noted, it takes at least two to two-and-a-half to three years from chip design to mass production; but model algorithms can change every six months. The reason: aggressive customization can boost efficiency 30-40% on Gemini models, but if the algorithmic paradigm shifts — beyond the core Transformer logic — rolling back is extremely painful. The fix: from V6 onward, training and inference split into two versions, with modular matrix units to fit different workloads; the software group's say has far exceeded the hardware group's. How serious? Watch out — the Transformer's first-mover advantage remains, but ASIC's generality trade-off is a long-term worry. As the guest said, before V6, they optimized Sparse Cores for recommendation ranking, sacrificing matrix density; at launch, the GPU's matrix compute actually looked better — that was a crisis version.

sentences.cn: 早期MoE在TPU上跑不好，因为2D拓扑下芯片只能与邻居通信，routing到不同专家需要绕很多环节。V4推出3D Torus+OCI光交换机，软件可编程配置通信路径，一次性解决MoE all-to-all痛点，效率明显提升
sentences.en: Early MoE didn't run well on TPUs, because in a 2D topology a chip can only talk to its neighbors, and routing to different experts required many detours. The V4 introduced a 3D Torus with an OCI optical switch, letting software program the communication paths, solving the MoE all-to-all pain point in one shot with a clear efficiency gain.
sentences.note: 表达提示MoE（Mixture of Experts）→ 专家混合模型；3D Torus → 三维环面拓扑；all-to-all → 全互联

scenes.title_cn: 五、供应链命门：博通与数据中心成本
scenes.title_en: The Supply-Chain Lifeline: Broadcom and Datacenter Costs
scenes.context: 博通在 TPU 供应链中的角色、GPU 与 TPU 的数据中心成本结构差异。语域：formal 供应链 + 成本分析。
scenes.speak: The core mechanism: the TPU team designs the chip's front end — the schematics; Broadcom handles the ICI interconnect, back-end signal layout, and mixed-signal work combining analog and digital — extremely high-barrier dirty work. Everything goes to TSMC for mass production. The key insight: Broadcom runs like a 2B business locked to its biggest customer, helping secure CoWoS and TSMC capacity; but its pricing power keeps growing, squeezing the TPU's margin. Without a backup plan — like Nvidia's bargaining position with TSMC — costs are hard to control. A typical scene: GPU clusters need a lot of expensive NVSwitch switches; the TPU uses barrel chips with direct connection plus a small amount of optical switching, and the datacenter build-out cost gap has already widened. As the episode put it, the GPU's main cost is switches; the TPU's main costs are liquid cooling and SerDes signal stability — and Broadcom is a very core link. Henry's conclusion: there's no absolute answer, but under the limited conditions of large-scale deployment, relatively stable models, and massive user bases sharing costs, the TPU can absolutely challenge the GPU. It's not suited for low-latency single-user agent scenarios — the more users, the faster inference gets, but you need enough batching to pack requests. As the episode put it, TPUs aren't well-suited for local deployment; they're great for operator-level use — scenarios like Gemini or ChatGPT with millions of daily users.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：TPU团队设计芯片前端（图纸），Broadcom负责ICI芯片互联、后端信号布局、混合信号（模拟+数字）——这是技术壁垒极高的「脏活」。最终交给TSMC量产
sentences.en: The core mechanism: the TPU team designs the chip's front end — the schematics; Broadcom handles the ICI interconnect, back-end signal layout, and mixed-signal work combining analog and digital — extremely high-barrier 'dirty work.' Everything goes to TSMC for mass production.
sentences.note: 表达提示ICI（Inter-Chip Interconnect）→ 芯片间互联；mixed-signal → 混合信号；dirty work → 脏活（高壁垒苦功）

sentences.cn: 关键理解：Broadcom像2B生意锁定最大客户，帮争取CoWoS/TSMC产能；但溢价权越来越大，TPU margin被挤压。没有backup方案（类似英伟达对台积电的议价）成本难控
sentences.en: The key insight: Broadcom runs like a 2B business locked to its biggest customer, helping secure CoWoS and TSMC capacity; but its pricing power keeps growing, squeezing the TPU's margin. Without a backup plan — like Nvidia's bargaining position with TSMC — costs are hard to control.
sentences.note: 表达提示pricing power → 溢价权；margin → 利润空间；bargaining position → 议价地位

sentences.cn: 典型场景：GPU集群需大量NVSwitch交换机（贵）；TPU用桶线芯片直连+少量光交换，数据中心建设成本已拉开差距
sentences.en: A typical scene: GPU clusters need a lot of expensive NVSwitch switches; the TPU uses barrel chips with direct connection plus a small amount of optical switching, and the datacenter build-out cost gap has already widened.
sentences.note: 表达提示NVSwitch → 英伟达交换芯片；optical switching → 光交换；build-out cost → 建设成本

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「GPU主要成本是交换机；TPU主要成本是液冷和SerDes信号稳定性，Broadcom是非常核心的环节」
sentences.en: As the episode put it: 'The GPU's main cost is switches; the TPU's main costs are liquid cooling and SerDes signal stability — and Broadcom is a very core link.'
sentences.note: 表达提示liquid cooling → 液冷；SerDes → 串行解串器；core link → 核心环节

sentences.cn: Henry结论：没有绝对答案，但在大规模部署+模型相对稳定+海量用户分摊成本的限定条件下，TPU完全可以挑战GPU。不适合单用户Agent低延迟场景——用户规模越大推理反而越快，但需要足够batch打包请求
sentences.en: Henry's conclusion: there's no absolute answer, but under the limited conditions of large-scale deployment, relatively stable models, and massive user bases sharing costs, the TPU can absolutely challenge the GPU. It's not suited for low-latency single-user agent scenarios — the more users, the faster inference gets, but you need enough batching to pack requests.
sentences.note: 表达提示batch requests → 批量打包请求；share the cost → 分摊成本；inference speed → 推理速度

sentences.cn: （引用）「TPU不太适合本地部署，很适合运营级使用——Gemini、ChatGPT这种每天millions of users的场景」
sentences.en: As the episode put it: 'TPUs aren't well-suited for local deployment; they're great for operator-level use — scenarios like Gemini or ChatGPT with millions of daily users.'
sentences.note: 表达提示local deployment → 本地部署；operator-level → 运营级；millions of daily users → 每日数百万用户

paraphrase.intent: 想说「GPU贵在交换机，TPU贵在液冷」
phrases: GPUs burn cash on switches; TPUs on cooling.
The two chips spend their money in different places.
paraphrase.chunks: burn cash on · spend money in different places

paraphrase.intent: 想说「TPU适合大规模不适合低延迟」
phrases: TPUs shine at scale, not at latency.
Great for millions of users, wrong for a single agent.
paraphrase.chunks: shine at scale · wrong for a single agent

scenes.title_en: A Decade of TPU Evolution and the Groq Rising Star
scenes.context: TPU 从 V1 到 V7 的进化脉络与 Groq 的差异化路线。语域：formal 技术史 + casual 故事。
scenes.speak: The V1 was an inference-only chip targeting CNN acceleration for search and recommendations, with Jeff Dean and David Patterson involved. The V2 became the flagship training chip, used for AlphaGo, AlphaFold, and early Transformers. The V4 added Sparse Cores for recommendation algorithms. The V5 and V6 entered the large-model era; the V6 split into training and inference versions, betting on Transformer pretraining. The V7 Ironwood, which Henry worked on, achieved 100% TPU training for Gemini. The origin story: in 2013, after Jeff Dean demonstrated a deep learning breakthrough, Jonathan Ross — now a Groq co-founder and Nvidia chief software architect — put up two slides: the good news that GPUs work, and the bad news that they couldn't afford it. If a user sent a three-minute voice message, datacenter costs would double — and that sparked the TPU self-research effort. Groq's founder Jonathan Ross comes from the TPU Compiler team, and Groq is essentially a compiler company rather than a chip company — what the LPU does every cycle is precisely determined by the compiler. It rode three waves: inference, low-latency ASICs, and the agent era with extreme tail-latency demands. The differentiation from TPU: Groq does small-scale local deployment with low latency, while the TPU does large-scale cloud throughput. As the episode put it, Groq is extremely fast once in use, because one person occupies a huge amount of LPU resources instead of sharing with many people.

sentences.cn: V1：仅Inference芯片，针对搜索推荐CNN加速（Jeff Dean、David Patterson参与）。V2：旗舰训练芯片，AlphaGo/AlphaFold/早期Transformer均用之。V4：加入Sparse Core服务推荐算法。V5/V6：进入大模型时代，V6分训练/推理两版本，押注Transformer预训练。V7 Ironwood：Henry参与，Gemini实现100% TPU训练
sentences.en: The V1 was an inference-only chip targeting CNN acceleration for search and recommendations, with Jeff Dean and David Patterson involved. The V2 became the flagship training chip, used for AlphaGo, AlphaFold, and early Transformers. The V4 added Sparse Cores for recommendation algorithms. The V5 and V6 entered the large-model era; the V6 split into training and inference versions, betting on Transformer pretraining. The V7 Ironwood, which Henry worked on, achieved 100% TPU training for Gemini.
sentences.note: 表达提示flagship training chip → 旗舰训练芯片；CNN（Convolutional Neural Network）→ 卷积神经网络；Jeff Dean → 杰夫·迪恩

sentences.cn: （引用）起源故事：2013年Jeff Dean演示深度学习突破后，Jonathan Ross（现Groq联合创始人、英伟达首席软件架构师）放两页PPT——「GPU能工作了（好消息）」「我们付不起这钱（坏消息）」，若用户发3分钟语音数据中心成本翻倍，由此催生TPU自研
sentences.en: The origin story: in 2013, after Jeff Dean demonstrated a deep learning breakthrough, Jonathan Ross — now a Groq co-founder and Nvidia chief software architect — put up two slides: 'GPUs work, the good news,' and 'we can't afford this, the bad news.' If a user sent a three-minute voice message, datacenter costs would double — and that sparked the TPU self-research effort.
sentences.note: 表达提示the good news / the bad news → 好消息/坏消息；spark → 催生；datacenter cost → 数据中心成本

sentences.cn: Groq创始人Jonathan Ross来自TPU Compiler团队，Groq本质是编译器公司而非芯片公司——LPU每个cycle做什么由编译器精准确定。踩中三轮：Inference→低延迟ASIC→Agent时代（对尾部延迟要求极高）。与TPU差异化：Groq做小规模本地部署低延迟，TPU做大规模云端吞吐量
sentences.en: Groq's founder Jonathan Ross comes from the TPU Compiler team, and Groq is essentially a compiler company rather than a chip company — what the LPU does every cycle is precisely determined by the compiler. It rode three waves: inference, low-latency ASICs, and the agent era with extreme tail-latency demands. The differentiation from TPU: Groq does small-scale local deployment with low latency, while the TPU does large-scale cloud throughput.
sentences.note: 表达提示compiler company → 编译器公司；ride the wave → 踩中浪潮；cloud throughput → 云端吞吐量

sentences.cn: （引用）「Groq一旦用起来会非常快，因为一个人占用非常多LPU资源而不是跟很多人共享」
sentences.en: As the episode put it: 'Groq is extremely fast once in use, because one person occupies a huge amount of LPU resources instead of sharing with many people.'
sentences.note: 表达提示occupy resources → 占用资源；share with others → 与别人共享

paraphrase.intent: 想说「TPU是谷歌被逼出来的」
phrases: The TPU was born from a cost scare.
Necessity, not ambition, created the TPU.
paraphrase.usage: necessity is the mother of invention 的变体

paraphrase.intent: 想说「Groq本质是编译器公司」
phrases: Groq is a compiler company wearing a chip's clothes.
Its hardware is just the compiler's puppet.
paraphrase.usage: wearing a chip's clothes 很形象

scenes.title_cn: 七、心法：如何理解TPU的真实竞争力
scenes.title_en: The Takeaway: How to Read the TPU's Real Competitiveness
scenes.context: 从软件栈视角理解 TPU 竞争力的心法，以及评估 TPU 前的落地清单。语域：formal 结论 + 实操建议。
scenes.speak: Why it matters: comparing only the Ironwood specs against the GB200 would mislead you — the TPU's value lies in the multiplier effect of XLA plus pod topology plus customized workloads; discussing the chip without its software stack is meaningless. The boundary: it fits fixed models, large scale, and accepting a hosted black box; it doesn't suit rapid algorithm experiments, single-user low-latency agents, or small teams without engineering talent. As the episode put it, compared to the chip, it depends more on the software; if you don't have someone who truly understands it internally, using Google Cloud might only reach 50-60% of the performance. How to apply it: before evaluating a TPU, first inventory whether your team has JAX and XLA experience; if not, prefer API access or stay with CUDA; if yes, when computing TCO, factor in the cost of Google's on-site support.

sentences.cn: 为什么重要：只看Ironwood参数对标GB200会误判——TPU价值在XLA+Pod拓扑+定制Workload的乘数效应；脱离软件栈谈芯片毫无意义
sentences.en: Why it matters: comparing only the Ironwood specs against the GB200 would mislead you — the TPU's value lies in the multiplier effect of XLA plus pod topology plus customized workloads; discussing the chip without its software stack is meaningless.
sentences.note: 表达提示multiplier effect → 乘数效应；pod topology → 集群拓扑；software stack → 软件栈

sentences.cn: 适用边界：模型固定+大规模+可接受托管黑盒；不适用于快速算法实验、单用户低延迟Agent、无工程团队的小团队
sentences.en: The boundary: it fits fixed models, large scale, and accepting a hosted black box; it doesn't suit rapid algorithm experiments, single-user low-latency agents, or small teams without engineering talent.
sentences.note: 表达提示hosted black box → 托管黑盒；rapid experiments → 快速实验；engineering talent → 工程能力

sentences.cn: （引用）「相比起芯片它更多依赖于软件；如果你内部没有特别懂的人，用谷歌云可能只能跑到50%到60%的性能」
sentences.en: As the episode put it: 'Compared to the chip, it depends more on the software; if you don't have someone who truly understands it internally, using Google Cloud might only reach 50-60% of the performance.'
sentences.note: 表达提示depend on software → 依赖软件；reach 50-60% of performance → 只能跑到五六成性能

sentences.cn: （引用）怎么落地：评估TPU前先盘点团队是否有Jax/XLA经验；无则优先API接入或继续CUDA；有则算TCO时需计入谷歌驻场支持成本
sentences.en: How to apply it: before evaluating a TPU, first inventory whether your team has JAX and XLA experience; if not, prefer API access or stay with CUDA; if yes, when computing TCO, factor in the cost of Google's on-site support.
sentences.note: 表达提示inventory → 盘点；API access → API接入；on-site support → 驻场支持

phrases: You can't judge the TPU by silicon alone.
The chip is only half the story; XLA is the rest.
paraphrase.chunks: by silicon alone · half the story
paraphrase.usage: only half the story 很地道

phrases: Without XLA expertise, skip the TPU.
No JAX people? Stay on CUDA.
paraphrase.chunks: skip the TPU · stay on CUDA
paraphrase.usage: skip / stay on 指令感强

practice.cn: 用「TCO」说：TPU的总体拥有成本可挑战英伟达。
practice.en: Under the right conditions, the TPU's total cost of ownership can challenge Nvidia's.
XLA is a black box — it squeezes performance, but external developers can't fix bugs alone.

practice.cn: 用「tail latency」说：TPU不适合低延迟场景。
practice.en: TPUs chase throughput, not tail latency — a single-user agent would feel the lag.

practice.cn: 用「yield rate」说：定制芯片良率不行就报废。
practice.en: If the yield rate is poor, a custom chip is scrapped — there's no downgrade path.

pitfalls.wrong: GPU is like a kitchen with many cooks, TPU is like water flowing in pipes.
pitfalls.right: GPUs are parallel chefs working independently; TPUs are an assembly-line relay with minimal scheduling.
pitfalls.why: 流水线比喻要说 assembly-line relay；water flowing 不准确，没有表达接力与调度。

pitfalls.wrong: TPU is faster than GPU in everything.
pitfalls.right: TPU beats GPU on TCO only under specific conditions — large-scale, stable models, shared costs.
pitfalls.why: 绝对化表达不对；要强调限定条件 limited conditions。

pitfalls.wrong: XLA is very difficult to use for outside developers.
pitfalls.right: XLA is a black box — outsiders can hardly debug it and must rely on Google engineers.
pitfalls.why: difficult to use 太委婉；用 black box + can hardly debug 才说透痛点。

pitfalls.wrong: Groq is a chip company like Nvidia.
pitfalls.right: Groq is essentially a compiler company — the LPU's every cycle is determined by its compiler.
pitfalls.why: Groq 本质是编译器公司；把它当芯片公司会误解其核心竞争力。

shifts.before: 以为TPU打不过GPU是天经地义
shifts.after: 限定条件（大规模+稳定模型+成本分摊）下 TPU 的 TCO 可以挑战英伟达
TPU 价值在 XLA+Pod 拓扑+定制 Workload 的乘数效应——软件栈决定性能天花板

shifts.before: 以为定制芯片越高性能越好
shifts.after: 激进定制是双刃剑：算法范式一变，回退极痛苦——通用性是长期隐忧
